language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hallo my name is Jorge. I am the cook in this underwater restaurant in the wreck of the Titanic.
Food is always a part of a food chain. The food chain shows who eats who.
For example: Algea are eaten by krill. Krill are eaten by small fish and the small fish are eaten by big fish. This means the big fish are on the top of the food chain.
Let's learn more on food chains!

dialog.text: It's all about eating and being eaten. Who is eating who? Place these animals in the correct spot in their food chain.
Help Jorge find the correct order of the different food chains by clicking on the correct text.
Wonderful!
At the beginning of all food chains is the sun. Sunlight is energy, and plants use this energy to grow. They grow bigger themselves, and they grow fruits. Therefore plants are called "producers".

Primary consumers are organisms that eat the producers:
they eat the plants.
We also call them herbivores.
Secondary consumers eat primary consumers: they eat other animals. We call them carnivores or meat-eaters.

Some animals eat both plants and meat, these animals are called omnivores. Tertiary consumers eat secondary consumers. Food chains "end" with top predators, animals that have few or no natural enemies and because of they are not eaten by others.

Small fish are not only eaten by big fish. Seagulls are also fond of them, and also penguins. Oh, and the whales too! So there are many different food chains. When you draw all the chains together you end up with a food web. Let's see if we can create a food web!
